title: MoSJE Pavilion at 45th IITF 2026 Records Sales of Approximately ₹2.07 Crore As on November 26; Strong Public Response Boosts Artisans’ Livelihoods
subtitle: Over 130 Artisans from 19 States Showcase India’s Rich Cultural Heritage , Traditional Craftsmanship, Strengthens Market Linkages, Entrepreneurship and Economic Empowerment
body_text: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s pavilion at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 has recorded cumulative sales of approximately ₹ 2.07 crore up to November 26, 2026 , reflecting an encouraging response from visitors and strong consumer appreciation for indigenous products, traditional craftsmanship and the entrepreneurial talent of artisans from across the country. Located at Hall No. 5, Ground Floor, ITPO, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, the Ministry’s pavilion has emerged as a vibrant platform for showcasing India’s diverse cultural heritage, traditional skills and indigenous craftsmanship. The enthusiastic participation of visitors and their purchases have provided direct market access to artisans and contributed to strengthening their livelihood opportunities. The Ministry’s participation at IITF 2026 reinforces its commitment to promoting inclusive economic development, preserving traditional craftsmanship, strengthening grassroots entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities towards the realisation of the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 . A Senior Official in the Ministry said more than 130 artisans from 19 States are participating in the fair through the Ministry’s three Apex Corporations, namely the National Scheduled Castes Finance and Development Corporation (NSFDC), the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) and the National Safai Karamcharis Finance and Development Corporation (NSKFDC). The participation of these Apex Corporations reflects the Ministry’s continued commitment to strengthening market linkages, promoting entrepreneurship and creating sustainable livelihood opportunities for artisans and entrepreneurs belonging to Scheduled Castes, Backward Classes, Safai Mitras and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNTs), he said. The Official said the pavilion features an extensive collection of traditional handlooms, intricately designed handicrafts, handcrafted jewellery, textiles, footwear, handmade articles and other indigenous products. He said representing the distinctive artistic identities and cultural diversity of different regions, these products provide visitors an opportunity to experience and appreciate India's rich traditions of craftsmanship. The encouraging sales performance underscores the importance of national-level exhibitions in enabling traditional artisans to enhance the visibility of their products, interact directly with customers, understand evolving consumer preferences, establish business networks and explore new market opportunities, the Official said. He added participation in such prestigious platforms also help artisans strengthen their entrepreneurial capabilities, expand their customer base and build sustainable business prospects. A significant highlight of the Ministry’s participation is the promotion of TULIP (Traditional Artisans’ Upliftment Livelihood Programme) , which aims to establish a distinct market identity for artisan-made products and enhance their recognition among consumers, the Official added. Through this initiative, the Ministry seeks to bridge the gap between traditional craftsmanship and contemporary market requirements, encourage innovation and create sustainable income-generating opportunities for artisans, he said. The Official said the Ministry’s efforts are aligned with the vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi under the guiding principle of ‘Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas’ , fostering inclusive growth, economic empowerment and equitable development. The Official remarked the 45th India International Trade Fair 2026, inaugurated on November 13, brought together producers, entrepreneurs, traders and consumers from across the country and abroad, providing a prominent platform for trade, commerce, entrepreneurship and cultural exchange. The Ministry’s pavilion has provided participating artisans with valuable exposure, enhanced market access and opportunities to connect with consumers. The encouraging response and sales achieved during the fair reaffirm the importance of providing traditional artisans with platforms to showcase their skills, promote their products and strengthen their economic self-reliance.
